newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: New Lithuanian government says to privatise more.
newsitem.headline: New Lithuanian government says to privatise more.

text.p: The new right-wing government in Lithuania on Wednesday promised it would expand the list of companies it intends to privatise in 1997.

"It is also intended to change in essence the privatisation programme of 1997, to expand the list of companies with bigger and more attractive firms," the government press office said in a statement after a cabinet meeting.
It did not say which firms would be added to the list.
Lithuania had a successful first wave of privatisation but the second stage of selling large companies became bogged down under the old government of former Communists.
New Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius, who leads a right-wing coalition formed from the Homeland Union party and the Christian Democrats, has pledged to speed up privatisation.
He has already pledged to sell Lithuanian Telecom but Western investors are also interested in the gas company, airline, ports and energy company.
Lithuania recently unveiled a list of 778 companies for sale that was drawn up under the previous government.
